question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{3\sqrt{5}} \\ 0 & -\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{4}{3\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $Q$ shown above. Find the matrix $R$ such that $A=QR$ is a QR factorization of $A.$
question.worked_solution:
Since $Q$ has orthonormal columns, pre-multiplying both sides of $A=QR$ by ${Q}^{T},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}^{T}\cdot A & ={Q}^{T}\cdot QR \\ {Q}^{T}\,A & =({Q}^{T}\,Q)R \\ {Q}^{T}\,A & ={I}_{2}R \\ R & ={Q}^{T}\,A\end{aligned}
$$

 

Note that ${Q}^{T}Q={I}_{2}$ since the columns of $Q$ are orthonormal.

Now, we calculate the matrix $R:$

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{3\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3} & -\frac{4}{3\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 0 & \frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
